title: fix: preserve explicit superRefine issue input
body:
`superRefine` currently uses nullish assignment when backfilling an issue's `input`, so an issue author who explicitly passes `input: null` or `input: undefined` has that value replaced with the parsed payload value when `reportInput` is enabled.

This switches the defaulting check to property presence in both `superRefine` paths, so omitted `input` still reports the parsed value while explicit nullish values are preserved. It also adds regression coverage for both `.superRefine(...)` and top-level `z.superRefine(...)` through `.check(...)`.

Validated with `pnpm test`, `pnpm lint:check`, and `pnpm format:check`.

reviews.body:
Nice catch, @frastefanini! The `??=` nullish assignment was silently swallowing explicit `null`/`undefined` inputs on issues — subtle but real bug.

**Review:**

1. **Root cause analysis**: Correct. `_issue.input ??= payload.value` replaces *any* nullish value with the parsed payload. Since `reportInput` docs say it "backfills" omitted input, explicit `null`/`undefined` should be preserved. ✅

2. **Fix**: `if (!("input" in _issue))` is the right approach — it checks property presence rather than value truthiness. Found in both `ZodTransform` (classic schemas.ts) and `_superRefine` (core/api.ts). ✅

3. **Tests**: Good coverage — tests both `.superRefine()` and `.check().superRefine()` paths, with three cases per test (default, explicit null, explicit undefined). ✅

4. **Edge cases considered**:
   - `issue.code` fallback is left as `??=` — correct, since `code` should never intentionally be null/undefined ✅
   - `reportInput: true` gating is covered (test uses it) ✅
   - The default case (omitted `input`) still gets the parsed value via the presence check ✅

5. **One question**: What happens when `reportInput` is false/not set? Looking at the code, `input` defaulting is gated internally — this change should not affect that path since the nullish coalescing in the issue construction itself is separate. Could be worth a test to confirm, but not a blocker.

Clean, well-scoped fix for a real bug. Welcome to open source! 🎉

> ✅ No new issues found. **Reviewed changes** — force-push to `009176d` with same fix swapping nullish coalescing (`??=`) for a property-presence check (`"input" in _issue`) in both `superRefine` paths, preserving explicit `input: null`/`undefined` on issues. - **Fix `_issue.input` backfill in `ZodTransform`** — `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/schemas.ts` replaces `_issue.input ??= payload.value` with `if (!("input" in _issue)) _issue.input = payload.value`. - **Fix `_issue.input` backfill in `_superRefine`** — `packages/zod/src/v4/core/api.ts` applies the same property-presence check. - **Regression test for `.superRefine()`** — `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/refine.test.ts` covers default, explicit `null`, and explicit `undefined` input. - **Regression test for `z.superRefine()` via `.check()`** — `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/index.test.ts` covers the top-level superRefine path.   ｜ [View workflow run](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/actions/runs/27405241518/job/80992671972) ｜ Using `DeepSeek Pro` (free via [Pullfrog for OSS](https://pullfrog.com/for-oss)) ｜ [𝕏](https://x.com/pullfrogai)
